description:
Most devs don't know this Cursor AI trick. It saves me 5 hours every single week.

The trick: custom rules file at the project root. Cursor reads it on every prompt and respects your codebase conventions automatically. No more reminding the AI about your folder structure, naming rules, or testing framework.

In this video: the exact rules file template, the 4 sections that matter most, and what to never include.

⚠️ Personal workflow. Adapt the rules to your codebase before copying.

scenes.voiceover: The problem: every prompt you waste tokens reminding Cursor about your folder structure, naming rules, and which framework you use.
scenes.visual_keyword: code editor file tree project structure
scenes.visual_prompt: Code editor showing project folder tree with nested directories, modern dark theme IDE, photorealistic

scenes.voiceover: The trick: create a file called dot cursor rules at the project root. Cursor reads it automatically on every prompt. Zero token waste.
scenes.visual_prompt: Code editor showing configuration file with project rules, syntax highlighted text, modern dark theme, photorealistic

scenes.voiceover: The 4 sections that matter: folder structure rules, naming conventions, testing framework, and forbidden patterns. Skip everything else.
scenes.visual_prompt: Modern interface showing 4 numbered configuration sections with checkmarks, clean UI design, photorealistic

scenes.voiceover: Real example: I told Cursor we use Vitest, not Jest. Every new test file now uses correct imports. No more manual rewrites.
scenes.visual_prompt: Code editor showing test file with green passing test indicators and Vitest framework imports, photorealistic

scenes.voiceover: Never include: API keys, secrets, or personal preferences. Rules file gets shared with team and may end up in version control.
scenes.visual_prompt: Security lock icon overlay on code editor with redacted secret keys, warning style, dark theme, photorealistic
